payload.vision_scope_stated: Complete in the M1 chain: inherited vision + phone delta (idea, to-be scene, goal priorities with the convenience-vs-security conflict resolved as v1 ruled), Moore pitch filled, scope = realize the inherited design on v2 against mock transport, non-goals = live pairing/from-away demo/live endpoint/secrets/Slack all explicitly out.
payload.problem_agreed: The delta is real and proven TODAY: the whole delegated run exists because a gate offer cannot reach an away owner - the delegation is the workaround standing in for this exact lane. The goal is worth having because from-away adjudication turns the 6h window from a stall risk into a one-tap decision, and because delegation should be a CHOICE the owner makes, not the only option when they step out.
payload.prior_art_positioned: Positioned against the field in adr-answer-authenticity's own comparison (HA context.id, LangGraph thread_id, gotoHuman meta) plus PagerDuty-style mobile ack: all take a correlation-id-possession ack (identical trust model to ours), but none produce a hash-bound, channel-stamped GRANT recorded beside desk blesses; raw ntfy sheds process; v1's own phone lane is the direct predecessor - it shipped and proved end-to-end, and this iteration re-realizes it on v2.
payload.success_measurable: Every need carries a mechanical pass line: a correct simulated tap -> a channel=phone grant bound to the offer hash (test); stale/duplicate taps -> unchanged grant chain (test); publish is a pure function to an injectable transport, mock-tested, no live topic touched (test); missing config -> graceful disable, no secret logged (test). The live from-away tap is the one owner-physical pass line, carried as a RAID trigger.
